newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Bosnia envoy says no guarantee of democratic vote.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia envoy says no guarantee of democratic vote.

text.p: Carlos Westendorp, the International High Representative in postwar Bosnia, said on Wednesday the OSCE was preparing well to monitor local elections in September but a truly democratic vote could not yet be guaranteed.
The envoy was speaking to reporters during a brief visit with Luxembourg's Foreign Minister Jacques Poos, whose country took over the European Union presidency for six months on July 1.
"I have seen the OSCE (Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe) working -- it is doing a great job. There are more than 2,000 monitors on the ground," Westendorp said.

"That will guarantee that the municipal elections are better than the general elections last year, but it won't guarantee in itself that the elections are completely democratic because there are not yet sufficient democratic elements (in Bosnia)..."
He said reforms of Bosnia's media and regional police forces, still tools of nationalist parties, were "two elements which are fundamental for these elections to be really democratic".

Westendorp was in Brussels earlier in the day to attend a donor conference where the international community pledged over $1.2 billion to help reconstruction in Bosnia this year following 43 months of war that ended in late 1995.
The envoy said that along with stability and security, economic reconstruction was one of the "fundamental pieces of the democratic process and of the wellbeing of Bosnia".
